newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Silvermines bids for Britain's CM Group.
newsitem.headline: Silvermines bids for Britain's CM Group.

text.p: Irish engineering and technology firm Silvermines Group Plc said on Monday that it had made a bid for UK-based Continental Microwave Group.

Silvermines said in a statement that the bid consisted of a 10 million stg initial cash consideration with an adjustment to be made after completion of an amount by which CM Group's net assets exceed or are less that 7.5 million stg.
The group said the maximum consideration payable is 14 million pounds.
Silvermines also announced a placing and open offer to raise approximately 12.6 million pounds after expenses.
The company has arranged for the placing of 16,805,775 new Silvermines shares at 78 Irish pence or 80 pence sterling with institutional and other investors.

Under the open offer, qualifying shareholders will be invited to subscribe for new Silvermines shares on the basis of 1 new share for every four held, at a price of 78 Irish pence or 80 pence sterling.
Silvermines said the placing and open offer was being initiated to facilitate the acquisition of CM Group.
CM Group consists of three companies -- CML and TRU-LON in the UK as well as RFT in the U.S.
Silvermines said the acquisition of CM fitted its strategy of being an electrical and electronics products and services business in a number of niche markets.

"CM Group is a world market leader in its specialised field of broadcast transmission equipment. We are confident that CM Group will benefit from our management approach and that there is considerable scope for improving CM Group's global marketing and improving its margins," Silvermines said.
Silvermines also announced a 17 percent increase in pre-tax profits for the six months to June 30, 1996, to 1.53 million pounds.
Turnover rose to 27.49 million sterling from 26.63 million in the same period a year earlier.
Silvermines announced a six percent increase in earnings per share to 1.72 pence sterling and declared an interim dividend of 0.35 pence per share.

The company said that current trading was in line with expectations and it anticipated that the performance in the second half of the year would benefit from the strong order intake in the first half.
